'''Brian L. Fisher''' (born 1964 or 1965)<ref name="revels">{{cite news|url=https://www.sfgate.com/magazine/article/Got-Ants-Entomologist-revels-in-studying-the-2718779.php|title=Got Ants? / Entomologist revels in studying the critters' fascinating ways|last=Whiting|first=Sam|date=10 October 2004|work=San Francisco Chronicle|access-date=21 November 2010}}</ref> is an American [[entomologist]] who works on the [[systematics]] of [[arthropods]], with a particular focus on [[ants]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Adventures+of+the+ant+man%3A+a+biologist+risks+life+and+limb+searching...-a0150864923|title=Adventures of the ant man: a biologist risks life and limb searching for ants|date=4 September 2006|work=Science World|accessdate=21 November 2010}}</ref> He has discovered over 1000 species, including 900 species of ants in [[Madagascar]].<ref name="revels" /> He mainly conducts field work in Madagascar and Africa.

==Career==
After working with the [[Smithsonian Institution]] in Panama, Fisher received a PhD on ant systematics at UC Davis.<ref name=revels/> He is the curator and chairman of the [[entomology]] department of the [[California Academy of Sciences]]. Fisher is also the present executive director of the Bibikely Biodiversity Institute and the [[Madagascar Biodiversity Center]].

In 2002, Fisher created [[AntWeb]], a database of ants. It costed [[United States dollar|US$]]30,000 to create.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dalton |first1=Rex |title=Ants join online colony to boost conservation efforts |journal=Nature |date=2003 |volume=424 |issue=6946 |page=242 |url=https://www.antweb.org/Nature_AntWeb_news.pdf |access-date=2024-06-04 |via=[[AntWeb]] |doi=10.1038/424242b |pmid=12867945 |bibcode=2003Natur.424..242D }}</ref>

He is known for naming ''[[Proceratium google]]'' after [[Google Inc.]]<ref name="Fisher">{{cite journal |last=Fisher |first=B. L. |year=2005 |title=A new species of ''Discothyrea'' Roger from Mauritius and a new species of ''Proceratium'' Roger from Madagascar (Hymenoptera: Formicidae) |journal=Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences |series=Fourth series |volume=56 |pages=657–667 |url=http://antcat.org/documents/4379/Fisher_2005_Proc_Calif_Acad_Sci.pdf}}</ref><ref name="Google">{{cite web |url=http://googleblog.blogspot.se/2005/09/ants-unearthed-with-google-earth.html |title=Ants unearthed with Google Earth |last=Fisher|first= Brian L. |date=30 September 2005 |website=Google Official Blog |accessdate=30 September 2005}}</ref>

The ant genus ''[[Fisheropone]]'' is named in his honour.

In 2016, Fisher launched IPSIO (Insects and People of the Southwest Indian Ocean). IPSIO was launched to develop a team approach to solving current conservation issues.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research |url=https://www.fisherlab.org/research.html |access-date=2026-08-18 |website=Brian L Fisher |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fisher grew up in [[Normal, Illinois]], and was inducted into the Pioneer Hall of Fame at [[Illinois State University]] Laboratory School.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.uhigh.ilstu.edu/alumni/awardwin/2001/brianfisher.html |title=Alumni Award Winners, 2001 |access-date=2011-09-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054904/http://www.uhigh.ilstu.edu/alumni/awardwin/2001/brianfisher.html |archive-date=2016-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
